stemMd: Which blood vessel carries oxygen-rich blood from the lungs to the left atrium of the heart?
explanationMd:
Follow the circuit. Oxygen-poor blood returns from the body through the venae cavae to the right atrium, passes to the right ventricle, and is pumped through the pulmonary trunk and the two pulmonary arteries to the lungs. There it picks up oxygen. Oxygen-rich blood returns through the pulmonary veins (normally four, two from each lung) to the left atrium, then passes to the left ventricle, and is pumped out through the aorta.

Remember that arteries carry blood away from the heart and veins carry blood towards it, whatever its oxygen content. So the pulmonary veins are veins that carry oxygen-rich blood, and the pulmonary arteries are arteries that carry oxygen-poor blood.

distractorRationale.e: The aorta leaves the left ventricle and carries oxygen-rich blood to the body. It does carry oxygen-rich blood, but away from the heart, not from the lungs to the left atrium.
distractorRationale.d: This assumes that the vessels linking the heart and lungs that matter for oxygen must be arteries. A pulmonary artery carries oxygen-poor blood from the right ventricle to a lung; it leaves the heart, which is why it is an artery, even though its blood is oxygen-poor.
distractorRationale.a: The superior vena cava is a vein entering the heart, but it carries oxygen-poor blood from the upper body to the right atrium, not from the lungs to the left atrium.
distractorRationale.b: The coronary arteries branch from the aorta and carry oxygen-rich blood away from the heart into its own wall. They do not bring blood from the lungs.

accessibilityText: A short text question with no figure. The question asks which blood vessel carries oxygen-rich blood from the lungs to the left atrium of the heart. The five choices are the superior vena cava, a coronary artery, a pulmonary vein, a pulmonary artery and the aorta.

provenance.notes: Original item on the pulmonary circuit. The distractors are the other named vessels that connect to the heart.

independentSolve.workingNotes: The pulmonary veins return oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium. The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs, the aorta leaves the left ventricle, the superior vena cava enters the right atrium, and the coronary arteries supply the heart muscle. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave7-resolve-held-run1) reached the same answer: The pulmonary veins carry oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium. The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs. The superior vena cava empties into the right atrium. The aorta leaves the left ventricle, and the coronary arteries supply the heart muscle.]
